answer: A farm must therefore either lie, which the jade graph proves on replay, or recruit 84 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the bridge registry records each claim and the meadow audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 37% of the attester's bond. That is 14 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
